name: Cadelling

attributes.attribute: a dynasty of early Wales made up of the descendants of Cadell
the Welsh kingdom where the later Cadelling were at home
the founding ancestor of the Cadelling line

sources: Jackson, Kenneth. Language and History in Early Britain. Edinburgh University Press, 1953.
text: Cadelling names a dynasty, the heirs of Cadell, in early Wales. The family rose in the north-east of the land. They appear in the praise verse of the Cynfeirdd. One poem calls Cynan Garwyn a man of the Cadelling line. By 829 the descendants sit in Powys. Their ancestor began as a low-born man who won the crown. A wicked tyrant named Benli fell by heavenly fire. St Germanus acted in that tale as the agent of change. Their first known king died at the battle of Chester. A rival house of Powys showed an open hatred for the Cadelling.

okr.objective: Present the Cadelling as a north-east Welsh royal dynasty of the early Middle Ages.
key_results: The dynasty appears in the early verse of the Cynfeirdd.
Its ancestor Cadell began as a low-born figure who took the crown.
